On 2026-02-26 the company guided 2026 capex of $30-35bn, which the CFO called 'more than double' 2025. CoreWeave lost $1.17bn on $5.13bn of revenue in FY2025, a net margin of about -23%, which fits a plain reading of 'deeply unprofitable'. One caveat: the operating loss was small (-1%), and most of the net loss was interest expense. 'Time bomb' is rhetoric and is not scored.
limitations: 'Deeply unprofitable' is true on net loss but not on operating loss.
On the company's $14.9bn accrual capex measure, $10bn understates 2025 spending.

our_interpretation: "Time bomb" is a rhetorical judgment and is not scored.
"Deeply unprofitable": plain reading is a large GAAP loss relative to revenue for FY2025. I use net loss, because that is what the company actually lost. I note that operating loss was small.
"$10bn in 2025": CoreWeave's cash purchases of property and equipment for 2025.
"Expected to double in 2026": the company's 2026 capex guidance, as of the post, was at least about twice the 2025 figure.
The target period covers FY2025 results and the guidance current when the post was published (through 2026-03-03).
criteria.support_condition: FY2025 shows a large loss, 2025 capex is about $10bn, and 2026 capex guidance as of the post is roughly double or more.
criteria.contradiction_condition: CoreWeave was profitable or only marginally loss-making on every measure, 2025 capex was far from $10bn, or 2026 guidance was well below double.
